items.slide_topic: Pipeline/constitution: Constitutional AI defined in one sentence (2022 paper)
items.dek: The only human oversight is provided through a list of rules or principles, and so we refer to the method as 'Constitutional AI'.
items.author: Yuntao Bai et al. (51 authors)
items.caption: Abstract of the Constitutional AI paper (Bai et al., submitted 15 Dec 2022)
items.notes: Loaded via export.arxiv.org API (published 2022-12-15T06:19:23Z) and the arxiv.org abs page via WebFetch. The ar5iv HTML lists 'Affiliation: Anthropic'. Simple one-sentence version for slides: Anthropic's 2022 Constitutional AI method trained a harmless AI assistant with no human labels for harmful outputs; the only human input was a written list of rules or principles, and the AI critiqued, revised and judged its own answers. The abstract's phrase 'without any human labels identifying harmful outputs' is also verbatim.

items.slide_topic: Pipeline/constitution: how Constitutional AI works (two stages)
items.dek: Both the critiques and the AI feedback are steered by a small set of principles drawn from a ‘constitution’.
items.author: Bai et al.
items.caption: Figure 1 of the Constitutional AI paper: supervised stage (red-team prompts, response, self-critique, revision, finetune SL-CAI model) then RL stage (AI-feedback preference model, RLAIF training, final RL-CAI model)
items.notes: Source image: ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2212.08073/assets/CAI-Overview.png (2025x844, unaltered copy). Viewed with Read. The figure is the paper's own diagram, not a mock-up. Dek is the verbatim caption sentence.

items.caption: Opening sentence of Claude's Constitution
items.notes: Verbatim first sentence of the constitution page. Companion 'why it matters' sentence, verbatim: 'It plays a crucial role in our training process, and its content directly shapes Claude’s behavior.'

items.slide_topic: Pipeline/constitution: the four priorities, in order
items.dek: In cases of apparent conflict, Claude should generally prioritize these properties in the order in which they’re listed.
items.caption: Ranking rule for conflicts between Claude's four priorities
items.notes: Verbatim from the announcement post's summary. The four priorities in listed order are: Broadly safe (not undermining appropriate human mechanisms to oversee AI during the current phase of development); Broadly ethical (being honest, acting according to good values, and avoiding actions that are inappropriate, dangerous, or harmful); Compliant with Anthropic's guidelines; Genuinely helpful (benefiting the operators and users they interact with). Same wording on constitution page.

items.dek: This document is likely to change in important ways in the future. … It is best thought of as a perpetual work in progress.
items.caption: Anthropic's own statement that the constitution may change and is a work in progress
items.notes: Two verbatim sentences from the constitution page's opening section, joined by an ellipsis where the middle sentences are omitted. Good for teen discussion of uncertainty.

items.dek: Our previous Constitution was composed of a list of standalone principles.
items.caption: Why the new constitution explains reasons instead of listing rules
items.notes: Verbatim from the announcement post. Reasons sentence (verbatim, same post): 'AI models like Claude need to understand why we want them to behave in certain ways'. Use for the rules-vs-reasons slide.

facts.claim: In 2022, Anthropic's Constitutional AI method trained a harmless AI assistant with no human labels identifying harmful outputs; the only human oversight was a written list of rules or principles.
facts.source: Bai et al., 'Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback' (arXiv 2212.08073), abstract

facts.claim: In Constitutional AI, the model critiques and revises its own answers, a model judges which of two answers is better, and those AI preferences train a reward model for reinforcement learning (RLAIF, 'RL from AI Feedback').
Anthropic published the new Claude constitution on Jan 22, 2026.
facts.source: Anthropic, 'Claude's new constitution' (page date and article:published_time 2026-01-22)

facts.claim: Anthropic released Claude's constitution in full under a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Deed, so anyone can use it for any purpose without asking permission.
facts.source: Anthropic, 'Claude's Constitution' page and announcement post

facts.claim: Anthropic says the constitution 'plays a crucial role in our training process, and its content directly shapes Claude's behavior'.
Claude's constitution ranks four properties for conflicts, in order: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, genuinely helpful.
Anthropic has used Constitutional AI in training Claude models since 2023; the previous constitution was 'a list of standalone principles', and the new one explains reasons.
Anthropic says its constitution 'is likely to change in important ways in the future' and is 'a perpetual work in progress'.
